object_description: compact rectangular atrium building with roof terrace
design_condition: The compact rectangular building divides the site into two open areas, strengthens a pedestrian axis with paired squares, and reserves space for a later extension while keeping the site traffic-free.

positive.statement: The simple large building and specific public outdoor spaces make an interesting urban-planning contribution.

position.target: large building and public outdoor spaces
position.rationale: The compact rectangular building and its central void visibly organize the sampled site geometry.

positive.statement: The protected outdoor workplace effectively showcases the institution's activities.

position.rationale: The central protected void is visible in plan and provides the best anchor for the outdoor workplace.

positive.statement: The building is clearly zoned, with prominent uses placed around the central area.

position.rationale: The sparse central opening is distinctly visible within the rectangular perimeter.

positive.statement: The flexible spatial layer supports different office, laboratory and practical-room configurations.

position.rationale: Repeated vertical bays and the compact floor plate support an approximate internal-layer placement.

positive.statement: The compact shape creates usable land reserves and a favourable floor-area-to-envelope ratio.

position.rationale: The rectangular envelope is clearly legible across the plan and all elevations.

positive.statement: The external appearance coherently corresponds to the rational floor plan and cubic structure.

position.rationale: The east facade clearly shows the regular cubic envelope and coherent vertical articulation.

negative.statement: After expansion, the remaining open areas would be overly open and mineral and would not meet all living needs.

position.rationale: The peripheral open strip beside the compact block is the plausible anchor for the expansion critique.

negative.statement: The basement delivery arrangement requires a deep intervention into the ground and is complex.

position.rationale: A low western edge location approximates the unshown ground-level delivery intervention.

negative.statement: The seminar-room floor has too little spatial quality because of its small foyer and long dark corridors.

position.rationale: The middle-lower portion of the tall block is used as a constrained seminar-floor anchor.

negative.statement: The ramp and cascade staircase meet problematically in a confined space, and the staircase feels too small at the exits.

position.rationale: The lower east-side circulation zone is the closest exterior anchor for the stair intersection.

negative.statement: Requiring access through employees' open-plan offices is viewed as unfavorable.

position.rationale: The western interior-facing bays provide a plausible approximate office-zone location.

negative.statement: The required floors and missing office and laboratory areas do not fit within the permitted building height.

position.target: required floors and missing office and laboratory areas
position.rationale: The full-height rectangular envelope visibly supports the building-height and program-capacity critique.

negative.statement: The entrance level appears depressed in its proportions because of the truss-girder facade.

position.rationale: The lowest south-facing band is the visible entrance-level surface.

negative.statement: The atrium concept is not entirely convincing in its interior implementation.

position.rationale: The central void is distinctly visible in plan, though its interior implementation is not resolved by the sample.
